questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanted to study in an english speaking country was the most important aspect. Another aspect was that wanted to study at a west coast university, preferably in Canada.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: University of Calgary was amazing

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The international service coordinator did a very good job at providing information upon arrival and was also very easy to get in contact with

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome center at the university which all international students could show up at, at any time. Here we were provided with information regarding getting around on campus and upcoming events.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy, us five people from KU arranged an airbnb together.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It took us around 15-30 minutes with bus to get to school, which was very easy. Look at the city transportation map to consider how far away from campus you are going to live, so you dont end up spending an hour getting to school.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not live a campus, but heard good things about it. The reason I did not live there was because I received the residence confirmation a month prior to departure (A lot of applications that year), so therefore I had already sorted out an airbnb.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: To register for most courses you have to get a prerequisite approval which is described relatively thoroughly on the university website

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: International student center, both physical and via email. They responded at least within 24 hours.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mildly successful, since not all courses that I intended to take was offered that semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look up previously offered courses for that type of semester (fx "Fall")

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only had 300- and 400-level courses, and the 400 level courses where clearly more difficult. The courses were still relatively easier than at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Depends on the size of the course. The 300-level courses were larger lectures, while 400-level courses were smaller classrooms.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Industrial Organization
Energy economics and policy
Electricity markets
Science and Philisophy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Industrial Organization was the most demanding and a high level course, but also very interesting and rewarding.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is relatively the same as Denmark, take-a-way is cheaper though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great fitness (gym) and sport facilities (squashm, badminton ect.)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Great fitness (gym) and sport facilities (squashm, badminton, basketball, football, hockey ect.)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for a club or participate in sports with other canadians or international students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Banff national park (Skiing, Hiking).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, people are VERY friendly

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very and open and friendly in general

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Just go, amazing place, with so much nature 
2. Show up a all social events in the beginning
3. Enjoy your time there, you will mostly have more spare time than at KU

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Social connections, skiing and nature

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: dont know

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
